one_month_reasoning: The window holds the biggest scheduled event of the quarter: Q3 2026 results on Oct 28 before the open [3]. Guidance was $0.70-0.71 post-split [2], and the Q3 consensus EPS estimate rose from $0.63 to $0.72 over 90 days [4]. That leaves a slightly higher bar for a beat than usual, but Amphenol has beaten and raised every quarter this cycle. Hyperscaler earnings and capex guides (MSFT/GOOGL/META/AMZN, late Oct) and the Oct 28 FOMC (Kalshi: 71% hold, 27% hike [11]) fall in the same week. Earnings-day moves over the last four reports were +3.6% (Oct-25), -12.2% (Jan-26, despite a beat), +3.2% (Apr-26) and +4.5% followed by +6% the next day (Jul-26) [17]. That shows fat tails in both directions, with an upward skew in frequency but a large downside when the bar is high. The stock also rallied about 10% off its mid-September low into the print. I use a near-symmetric spread with fat tails: monthly sigma of about 12.5% (between the 46%/3.5 rule of 13% and the longer-run lower vol), widened in the tails for the earnings event, and a small +0.7% drift for positive estimate revisions and momentum. That gives P(>=85.67) of about 0.52.

fair_value.method: Blend of (a) 2028E EPS of about $3.70 x 25x forward P/E = $92.5; (b) Oct-2027 trailing EPS of about $3.05 x the 30x 10-year median trailing P/E = $91.5; (c) a base-rate-anchored drift of +8% from $85.67 = $92.5. Weights 0.5/0.3/0.2.

APH's own history is a survivor's (it compounded about 27% a year). I haircut the median toward a typical large-cap +7-9% and keep the 2000-02 analog in the left tail: APH fell about 52% from its Oct-2000 peak to Sep-2002, and 53% peak-to-trough in 2008 [6,15]

bear.story: AI capex digestion or bubble deflation (Polymarket 18% by mid-2027 [10]) and/or a US recession (Polymarket 35% by end-2027 [9]). Orders roll over from a book-to-bill of 1.23 [1], 2028E EPS is cut to about $2.9, and the multiple de-rates to about 20x, the hardware median plus a premium [8]. That is a drawdown of about 30%, the 5th-to-10th percentile of APH's own history and milder than 2001/2008 thanks to the diversified harsh-environment and industrial mix [6,15].

base.story: Hyperscaler capex keeps growing into a $1.0-1.3T 2027 [13,14], EPS tracks consensus ($3.29 for 2027) with modest beats, and the multiple drifts down from about 27x to 25x forward as growth slows and rates stay firm [11]. EPS growth roughly offsets de-rating and the stock grinds up about 7%.

bull.story: Beat-and-raise continues (estimate revisions are still rising: 2027 EPS went from $2.86 to $3.29 in 90 days [4]), 2028E EPS reaches about $4.1, a China tariff deal holds [12], and the market keeps a ~30x forward multiple as the AI connectivity share story extends. The stock would be near the top of the analyst range ($115) and beyond [5].

thesis_break_reason: A close below about $62 (-28%) would put APH below the March-May 2026 lows ($59-63) that held through the Q1 guide-down scare [16,17]. At about 19x 2027E EPS it would be near the hardware-sector median [8] and the bottom of the 10-year P/E range [7]. Getting there almost certainly needs estimate cuts (an order roll-over or a hyperscaler capex cut), not just multiple drift, so I would treat it as fundamental rather than ordinary volatility.

reasoning: Anchor: APH's own 30-year history gives a median 12m forward return of about +22% after a +25-60% year, with 20% of cases negative and a 5th percentile of -27% [6]. That record is a survivor's, so I haircut the median toward large-cap norms (+7-9%) and fatten the left tail with the 2001 telecom bust and 2008 analogs (-52% / -53%) [6,15]. Fundamentals: 2026E EPS is $2.67 and 2027E is $3.29 post-split [4]. Q2 sales grew 30% organically with a book-to-bill of 1.23 [1], so near-term momentum is strong. Today's 41x TTM and about 27x forward P/E sit 37% above the 10-year median trailing P/E [7,8], so I assume EPS growth is partly absorbed by de-rating. Fair value is about $92 (P/E on 2028E, P/E on mean-reverted trailing, base-rate drift). Macro and event odds are mixed. Polymarket prices a 35% recession by end-2027 [9], 18% for an AI bubble burst by mid-2027 [10] and about 93% for a US-China tariff deal by year-end [12]. Kalshi leans toward the next Fed move being a hike [11]. Consensus hyperscaler capex of $1.0-1.3T in 2027 supports the base case [13,14]. My mixture is bear 22% at $58, base 53% at $92 and bull 25% at $122, each with lognormal dispersion. It implies a median of about $91, a mean of about $94 and a log standard deviation of about 0.35. That is below the 46% realized vol because the longer-run monthly vol is 25-33% [6]. The result is P(>= today's $85.67) of about 0.58.
